title: Buying a train ticket
setting: You're at the staffed ticket window (みどりの窓口) at a JR station, heading to Kyoto.

options.japanese: 京都までお願いします。
options.feedback: Destination + までお願いします. This opens the whole transaction in four words.
Fine as an opener, though they've already invited you forward — you can go straight to the destination.
Not wrong, but you have the Japanese for this. Leading with the English question skips the part you can actually do.

n2.speaker: staff
n2.japanese: 片道ですか、往復ですか。
n2.romaji: Katamichi desu ka, ōfuku desu ka.
n2.audioHint: かたみちですか、おうふくですか

options.feedback: Repeating the half of the question you want is the cleanest way to answer an either/or in Japanese.
Same pattern. 往復 is usually cheaper than two singles.
はい can't answer an either/or question — there's nothing to say yes to. This is the single most common mistake with this question shape.

n2b.speaker: staff
n2b.japanese: えっと…片道ですか？往復ですか？
n2b.romaji: Etto… katamichi desu ka? Ōfuku desu ka?
n2b.audioHint: えっと、かたみちですか、おうふくですか

options.feedback: Recovered. Naming the option you want is always unambiguous.
Also a fine recovery — buying yourself a repeat is never a wrong move.

n3.speaker: staff
n3.japanese: 指定席と自由席、どちらになさいますか。
n3.romaji: Shiteiseki to jiyūseki, dochira ni nasaimasu ka.
n3.english: Reserved or unreserved seat, which would you like?
n3.audioHint: していせきとじゆうせき、どちらになさいますか

options.feedback: Reserved. Worth it on a holiday weekend or with luggage — you're guaranteed a seat.
Unreserved, cheaper, and usually fine off-peak. 〜でいいです is a useful 'that one's fine' for any offered choice.
Reasonable instinct — reserved costs more — but it stalls the transaction. Ask おすすめは？ or just pick one and ask the price at the end.

n4.speaker: staff
n4.japanese: 一万三千八百二十円です。

furigana.r: いちまんさんぜんはっぴゃくにじゅうえん

n4.romaji: Ichiman sanzen happyaku nijū en desu.
n4.audioHint: いちまんさんぜんはっぴゃくにじゅうえんです

options.feedback: JR ticket windows all take cards. Note the 一万 — Japanese counts in units of 10,000, so this is 'one man, three thousand…'.
No shame in it. Long prices come fast, and they'll also point at the display showing the figure.

n5.speaker: staff
n5.japanese: はい、切符です。三番線から発車します。
n5.romaji: Hai, kippu desu. Sanbansen kara hassha shimasu.
n5.english: Here's your ticket. It departs from platform 3.
n5.audioHint: はい、きっぷです。さんばんせんからはっしゃします

options.feedback: Caught the platform number. 三番線 — the 番線 counter is worth recognising instantly.
They already said it, but confirming a platform number is never a bad idea when a train costs ¥13,820.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Ticket in hand, platform known. The either/or question at n2 is the one to drill — はい genuinely doesn't answer it.
